title: Project Card v1
description: Project anchor: definition, purpose, scope, stakeholders, and current status. One per project folder as project.json. The coach reads this to ground every meeting analysis in the project's overarching goal — without a project card, the coach starts every session by collecting this information and then writes the card.

schema_version.description: Project-card schema version. v1 is the initial version (English, coach-scoped).

id.description: Format: {customer_code}-{project_code}. No user prefix — the project card is a shared artifact. Examples: ACME-CLOUD, STOWLINE-ETL, NRTH-PORTAL.

purpose.description: 1-3 sentences: why are we doing this project? What does it solve? Hard non-empty — prevents empty metadata. The coach refers back to this when a meeting drifts from the project's reason for being.

in_scope.description: 3-6 bullets: what falls within the project's scope.

out_of_scope.description: Bullets: what is explicitly out of scope. May be empty.

success_criteria.description: Measurable statements at the project level. Required once status is execution, golive, aftercare, or done.

status.description: Lifecycle phase. Drives the coach's prior on what facilitation challenges to expect (e.g., initiation meetings hinge on alignment; aftercare on accountability).

since.description: Since when has the project been at this level (duration signal).

health.description: Project health signal, separate from status. Yellow/red projects need more direct coaching on hard conversations.

code.description: Short code used in the project id (e.g., ACME, STOWLINE).

industry.description: Optional. Context for the coach (e.g., 'healthcare', 'fintech', 'public sector').

stakeholders.description: Key people across customer, vendor, and internal sides. The coach uses this to recognize attendees in meeting-cards and notice patterns (e.g., 'the sponsor has not been in any of the last four meetings'). When contact_id is set, the contact-card is the authoritative source — name/role here are convenience copies.

contact_id.description: Optional reference to a contact-card. If set, the contact-card is the canonical record; if null, this stakeholder lives only on the project-card.

role.description: Role on the project, e.g., 'project sponsor', 'tech lead', 'vendor PM', 'customer PMO'.

decision_authority.description: Optional RACI-style hint. Helps the coach notice when decisions are being made without the right people in the room.

timeline.description: Optional. The coach uses this to gauge time-pressure context — deadline-pressured meetings facilitate differently than open-ended ones.

risks.description: Short list of top project risks. The coach uses these to recognize when a meeting is dancing around the elephant.

meetings_glob.description: Optional glob pattern to find meeting-cards for this project, e.g., 'meetings/MTG-ACME-CLOUD-*.json'.
